reason: The cited evidence (E1) confirms that 0.6 wt.% Nb gives the best corrosion resistance and a duplex oxide layer forms, but it does not provide any data or discussion on grain boundary refinement, diffusion kinetics, or the specific detrimental phases from excess Nb. Thus, the mechanistic premises about microstructure and diffusion are unsupported.
premises: Nb addition around 0.6 wt.% refines grain boundaries in AFA steels
Refined grain boundaries facilitate controlled diffusion of Cr and Al to the surface
This diffusion leads to a dense duplex oxide layer (outer Cr2O3, inner Al2O3)
Excess Nb (>0.6 wt.%) forms detrimental Fe-rich nodules and secondary phases
Too little Nb fails to enhance diffusion kinetics effectively
